subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If n is an integer and z = cis θ, then show that (z²ⁿ − 1)/(z²ⁿ + 1) = i tan nθ.

mark_split.label: Reduce the numerator with double angles
Reduce the denominator with double angles

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — what De Moivre's theorem gives for z²ⁿ, which double-angle identities reduce the numerator and the denominator, and what cancels at the end.
insider_note: The one move this question depends on is writing −2 sin² nθ as 2i² sin² nθ. Without it the numerator will not factor and nothing cancels.

steps.label: z²ⁿ by De Moivre
steps.margin_note: First mark. z²ⁿ = cos 2nθ + i sin 2nθ. Write the numerator as cos 2nθ − 1 + i sin 2nθ and the denominator as cos 2nθ + 1 + i sin 2nθ on separate lines; the two reductions that follow take one at a time.
lines: z = cis θ = cos θ + i sin θ

recall.must_convey: That z to the 2n is cos 2nθ + i sin 2nθ by De Moivre's theorem, and this is put into the numerator and the denominator.
accept: z to the two n is cos two n theta plus i sin two n theta by De Moivre, substitute it in top and bottom
apply De Moivre to get cis two n theta and write the numerator and denominator
the power two n goes onto the angle, then put it into the fraction
De Moivre tho z power two n cis two n theta, daanni fraction lo pettali
numerator is cos two n theta minus one plus i sin two n theta

steps.why: De Moivre's theorem turns z²ⁿ into a single cosine and sine of the angle 2nθ. Writing the numerator and the denominator on separate lines sets up the two half-angle reductions that follow.
common_mistakes: Writing z²ⁿ = cos²ⁿ θ + i sin²ⁿ θ, which is false.
Forgetting the −1 in the numerator or the +1 in the denominator.
Trying to divide the two cis forms directly without the half-angle step.

steps.label: Reduce the numerator
steps.margin_note: Second and third marks. cos 2nθ − 1 = −2 sin² nθ and sin 2nθ = 2 sin nθ cos nθ. Write the −2 as 2i², and 2i sin nθ comes out leaving cos nθ + i sin nθ inside — the same bracket the denominator will produce.
lines: Numerator = −2 sin² nθ + 2i sin nθ cos nθ
= 2i² sin² nθ + 2i sin nθ cos nθ  (∵ i² = −1)
= 2i sin nθ (i sin nθ + cos nθ)
= 2i sin nθ (cos nθ + i sin nθ)

recall.must_convey: That cos 2nθ − 1 = −2 sin² nθ and sin 2nθ = 2 sin nθ cos nθ, so the numerator factors as 2i sin nθ (cos nθ + i sin nθ).
accept: cos two n theta minus one is minus two sin squared n theta, and the numerator factors to two i sin n theta times cis n theta
use the double angle formulas, write minus two as two i squared, and take out two i sin n theta
the numerator becomes two i sin n theta into cos n theta plus i sin n theta
double angle use chesi two i sin n theta bayataki teeyali, bracket lo cis n theta migulutundi
minus two sin squared is two i squared sin squared, then factor out two i sin

steps.why: The move that makes the fraction cancel is writing −2 as 2i². Then both terms of the numerator share the factor 2i sin nθ, and what is left inside the bracket is exactly cos nθ + i sin nθ, the same bracket the denominator will produce.
common_mistakes: Using cos 2nθ − 1 = 2cos² nθ − 2, which does not factor with the sine term.
Taking out 2 sin nθ instead of 2i sin nθ and leaving a bracket that does not match the denominator's.
Writing the bracket as (i sin nθ + cos nθ) and not recognising it as cis nθ.

steps.label: Reduce the denominator
steps.margin_note: Fourth and fifth marks. cos 2nθ + 1 = 2 cos² nθ, so the denominator is 2 cos² nθ + 2i sin nθ cos nθ = 2 cos nθ (cos nθ + i sin nθ). Take out the 2 as well as cos nθ, or it will not cancel.
lines: Denominator = 2 cos² nθ + 2i sin nθ cos nθ
= 2 cos nθ (cos nθ + i sin nθ)

recall.must_convey: That cos 2nθ + 1 = 2 cos² nθ, so the denominator factors as 2 cos nθ (cos nθ + i sin nθ).
accept: cos two n theta plus one is two cos squared n theta, so the denominator is two cos n theta times cis n theta
use the double angle formula and take out two cos n theta
the denominator becomes two cos n theta into cos n theta plus i sin n theta
one plus cos two n theta two cos squared, two cos n theta bayataki teeste cis n theta migulutundi
factor two cos n theta from the bottom

steps.why: 1 + cos 2A = 2cos² A is the partner of the numerator's identity. Taking out 2 cos nθ leaves the same bracket cos nθ + i sin nθ, which is what allows the cancellation.
common_mistakes: Using 1 + cos 2nθ = 2 sin² nθ, the wrong identity.
Taking out only cos nθ and leaving a 2 that then does not cancel.
Writing the bracket as (cos nθ − i sin nθ) by copying the wrong sign.

steps.label: Cancel and conclude
steps.margin_note: Sixth and seventh marks. The 2 and the bracket cos nθ + i sin nθ are common to both lines and cancel, leaving i sin nθ / cos nθ = i tan nθ. Keep the i; without it the answer is tan nθ, which is not the right side.

lines.text: \text{L.H.S.} = \frac{2i\sin n\theta\,(\cos n\theta + i\sin n\theta)}{2\cos n\theta\,(\cos n\theta + i\sin n\theta)}

recall.must_convey: That the common bracket (cos nθ + i sin nθ) and the 2 cancel, leaving i sin nθ / cos nθ = i tan nθ.
accept: the bracket cos n theta plus i sin n theta cancels top and bottom leaving i sin over cos which is i tan n theta
cancel the common factors and we get i tan n theta
after cancelling the two and the bracket the result is i tan n theta
common bracket cancel ayyi i sin n theta by cos n theta, that is i tan n theta
i sin n theta over cos n theta equals i tan n theta which is the right side

steps.why: Both reductions were aimed at producing the same bracket so that it cancels. What survives is i times sine over cosine, which is i tan nθ — the right-hand side.
common_mistakes: Cancelling the bracket but forgetting to cancel the 2, leaving 2i tan nθ.
Dropping the i and writing tan nθ.
Writing sin nθ / cos nθ = cot nθ.
